objective: In this workspace, make Wonderland's Social Hub keep the player's scroll position through a server refresh. `wonderland/Source/Wonderland/WonderlandSocialHubPanel.cpp` rebuilds its body on every refresh (the 20-second poll and every social event), and every rebuild makes NEW scroll boxes: a scrolled FRIENDS, REQUESTS, RECENT, PARTY or MESSAGES-inbox list jumps back to the top, and the open conversation is forced to its newest line, so older messages cannot be read past one refresh. Implement the scroll memory, and the six QA hooks that `wonderland/Source/Wonderland/WonderlandSocialHubScrollQa.cpp` calls, by editing `WonderlandSocialHubPanel.cpp` and `WonderlandSocialHubPanel.h` in place. That QA file is the acceptance test: it is read-only here and it is NOT compiled here. This workspace cannot build Unreal; after this mission the game's own pipeline applies your change, compiles it and runs the QA.
requirements: Declare these six functions, exactly as written, in the PUBLIC part of `SWonderlandSocialHubPanel` in `WonderlandSocialHubPanel.h`, and define each exactly once in `WonderlandSocialHubPanel.cpp`: `float QaListScrollOffset() const;` `bool QaSetListScrollOffset(float Offset);` `float QaHistoryScrollOffset() const;` `bool QaSetHistoryScrollOffset(float Offset);` `bool QaHistoryAtEnd() const;` `void QaSetScrollMemory(bool bOn);`. What each one means is stated in the header comment of `WonderlandSocialHubScrollQa.cpp`.

THE MAIN LIST. A REFRESH (SetSnapshot, then the deferred rebuild that FlushRebuild or Slate's pre-tick runs) keeps the open tab's main list at the offset the player left it: FRIENDS, REQUESTS, RECENT, the MESSAGES inbox, or PARTY's party list. The voice people list on PARTY is not a main list.
THE HISTORY. A refresh keeps the open conversation's history at the offset the player scrolled back to. When the player was at its end, the history stays at its end and follows new messages.
The memory never crosses conversations: when a refresh leaves a DIFFERENT conversation open (for example because the open one is no longer in the snapshot), that conversation starts at its end.
The player's own OpenConversation (a click on a conversation row) opens that conversation at its END, whatever was remembered, also when it is already the open one.
`QaSetScrollMemory(false)` restores the pre-fix behaviour EXACTLY: every rebuild starts the lists at the top and the history at its end. The memory is ON by default.

`QaListScrollOffset` and `QaHistoryScrollOffset` return the open tab's main list's and the open conversation's `SScrollBox::GetScrollOffset()`. `QaSetListScrollOffset` and `QaSetHistoryScrollOffset` scroll as a player would (`SScrollBox::SetScrollOffset`) and return false when the open tab draws no main list, or no conversation is open. `QaHistoryAtEnd` is true when the history's offset is within 1.0 Slate unit of `SScrollBox::GetScrollOffsetOfEnd()`; it is meaningful only after a layout.
Out of scope, any behaviour is acceptable: what a tab switch does to scroll positions, and the voice people list on PARTY.

F-21 STAYS INTACT. SetSnapshot and SetVoice still only ASK for a rebuild (RequestRebuild) and never rebuild at once. RequestRebuild, HandleSlatePreTick and FlushRebuild keep their bodies. Construct still registers `OnPreTick().AddSP(this, &SWonderlandSocialHubPanel::HandleSlatePreTick)` and the destructor still removes it. The reply draft carry stays: `ReplyDraftConversationId` remains, and Rebuild still clears `bRebuildPending` and still records `ReplyDraftConversationId = OpenConversationId;`.

The QA code at the foot of `WonderlandSocialHubPanel.cpp`, from the line `namespace WonderlandSocialBlockedQa` to the end of the file, is not edited at all, so `wl.Qa.SocialHubClicks` still reads 9 pass / 0 fail. Put new code above it.

UNREAL ENGINE 5.8 SScrollBox, as installed (the same facts head the QA file): `GetScrollOffset` returns the DESIRED offset, unclamped. `SetScrollOffset` stores it at once, clears a pending ScrollToEnd and does not clamp, so it is honoured on a NEW box before its first layout. `ScrollToEnd` only sets a flag that the box's Tick resolves from its geometry, so before a layout `GetScrollOffset` still reads the old value (0 on a new box). `GetScrollOffsetOfEnd` uses the box's cached geometry, so it is meaningful only after a layout. Use only these members of SScrollBox and the ones the file already uses.
